transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-10
- Start: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Ironbridge Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Priya Gupta (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood did a security posture discovery. Ironbridge asked about SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integrations, data residency and retention windows. Conversation covered hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options and tradeoffs (latency vs cost, isolation). Next steps include sharing SOC2 artifacts, network diagrams, scheduling technical deep dive and a benchmark, and sending pricing.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO27001)
- Authentication/SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC
- Audit logging, retention, and exportability
- Encryption and KMS/HSM options for Private/Dedicated
- Data residency and retention policy for embeddings and logs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you making time. Jonah and I are from Redwood, we'll run through security posture questions and then Jonah can dig into architecture.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi thanks, I'm aisha, heading security at Ironbridge. We've been evaluating vendors for an embeddable LLM service, main things are compliance and control, we have regulatory clients so this is high priority.
[00:20] Liam: Hey all, liam here, platform, I'll be the one integrating. We care about network isolation and key mgmt.
[00:26] Priya: Priya from procurement, here to understand timelines and contract stuff.
[00:30] Jonah: Great. Quick agenda: confirm compliance artifacts, SSO and RBAC, encryption/KMS, audit logs and retention, then discuss deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and follow-ups.

[02:05] Aisha: First, do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001? We need the report and scope. Also are there any subservice orgs, is data stored in third-party services?
[02:18] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. I'll share the attestations and the control mapping. There's a link to the auditor report — it's hosted in our compliance portal. For hosted we do use cloud providers for compute and storage, but Redwood controls access and we've got contractual terms and subprocessors listed.
[02:34] Aisha: Okay, we'll need the actual report and also the controls mapping to our requirements. Can you include retention of logs and where audit logs land?

[04:00] Jonah: On audit logs, for hosted we surface request-level logs and admin activity. Logs are pushed to a managed logging pipeline; we can export via S3 or syslog to your SIEM. Retention defaults to 90 days but can be extended. For Dedicated and Private deployments, logs can be kept in your environment only.
[04:26] Liam: Export via S3 is good, can you confirm encryption of logs at rest? And are the logs PII redacted by default?
[04:39] Jonah: Logs are encrypted at rest using provider-managed encryption, and when exporting we support SSE-KMS for S3 uploads. Regarding PII redaction, we do not automatically redact model output; that's usually handled at integration time. We do support configurable logging levels so you can disable full request logging.

[06:15] Aisha: For encryption of customer data at rest, we need customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM integration. What's your approach?
[06:25] Maya: For Hosted we support KMS integration — you can bring your own KMS in some enterprise plans (Dedicated/Private can integrate with your KMS or HSM). For Dedicated, we also offer an HSM-backed key option via our managed appliances if needed. We'll share the exact key flow diagram.
[06:44] Jonah: To add, our runtime can be configured so that model weights and ephemeral caches are encrypted, and the KV cache can be stored in your encrypted datastore for Private deployments. For hosted, the KV cache lives in managed infra but can be configured for encryption and rotation policies.

[08:10] Aisha: SSO is next. We use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. We need RBAC and session controls. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP and enforce SAML/SCIM?
[08:22] Maya: Yes — Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We have RBAC with role templates (admin, developer, viewer) and you can map IdP groups to roles. We also support session timeout controls and 2FA enforcement via the IdP.
[08:40] Liam: Does the RBAC extend to model-level permissions and route-level keys? We want least privilege so some services only get embeddings and not generation.
[08:51] Jonah: Good Q. We support per-team and per-route API keys and token scoping. You can bind keys to models, quotas, and routes. For Dedicated and Private you can enforce network policies so only certain subnets can reach the runtime.

[11:05] Aisha: Auditability: do you provide immutable audit logs and tamper evidence? We need to ensure logs can't be modified post-ingest.
[11:18] Jonah: We write immutable event streams into write-once storage and provide checksums. For hosted we supply signed audit bundles and you can pull them via the API. In Dedicated/Private the logs exist in your environment and you control retention and immutability policies.
[11:33] Aisha: Good. Also chain-of-custody for data access — who at Redwood can access customer data?
[11:42] Maya: Access is strictly role-based. Customer data access by Redwood employees requires approvals and is logged. We also have privileged access workflows, break glass with justification, and quarterly access reviews.

[13:05] Priya: On data residency, we have European clients. Do you support regionally isolated hosting and how do you certify data stays in-region?
[13:18] Jonah: We operate regional hosting. For hosted we can pin workloads to EU regions. For Dedicated and Private, obviously you deploy into your region. We have documentation on data flow and subprocessors by region — we'll include that.

[15:10] Aisha: Retention policies: embeddings and model outputs — how long do you keep them? Is there per-customer retention?
[15:22] Jonah: By default, hosted ephemeral request data is kept short for 7 days for debugging and 90 days for logs; embeddings and persistent artifacts are configurable. For privacy-sensitive customers we offer zero retention mode or customer-controlled retention windows. Dedicated/Private give you full control.

[17:40] Liam: For Dedicated, what's the network topology? Do we have VPC peering or PrivateLink? Also how are updates handled (patching, OS/kernel)?
[17:50] Jonah: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink options. Patching is coordinated — we schedule maintenance windows; for critical security patches we have emergency procedures. Patches are applied to the host OS and runtime; we provide images and change logs. For Private (on-prem) you manage the host patches or we provide air-gapped upgrade bundles if requested.

[19:15] Aisha: Can you walk briefly through the encryption flow for keys when using customer-managed KMS? I'm thinking about key usage logs and separation of duties.
[19:26] Jonah: Sure: with CMK, keys stay in your KMS — Redwood services call the KMS for envelope encryption operations; we never store plaintext of the root keys. Key usage is logged in your KMS and we provide correlation IDs in our logs so you can match operations. For HSM, we can integrate via standard PKCS#11 or cloud HSM APIs.

[21:30] Maya: A quick question from procurement — general timeline and proof-of-concept?
[21:36] Priya: Yes, timeline, cost estimate for pilot, and contract basics (SLA, liability).
[21:40] Maya: We'll send a pilot pricing estimate for both hosted pilot and Dedicated reserve. SLA details are in our enterprise agreement — we'll highlight uptime, support response times and penalties.

[23:55] Aisha: Any third-party pen testing? We require vendor penetration testing reports or attestation.
[24:04] Jonah: We do annual 3rd-party pen tests and can share executive summaries; for higher risk customers we can coordinate targeted assessments under NDA.

[25:30] Liam: Performance: if we run a benchmark, what's the best way to measure latency for small prompt/large prompt scenarios? We want tail latency numbers.
[25:42] Jonah: We'll run a workload with representative prompt length distribution. For Dedicated we can do reserved throughput tests in your tenancy or a staging environment. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token. We'll also demonstrate batching and KV cache impact.

[28:10] Aisha: Any built-in DLP or filtering to prevent model hallucinated PII leakage?
[28:22] Jonah: We have configurable output filters and can integrate with DLP pipelines; however, content-level PII suppression usually happens at integration layer. We can show patterns for redaction and user-level masking in the deep-dive.

[31:00] Maya: Wanted to flag a few common compliance asks — long-term retention alignment, exportability of logs for audits, and contractual language for data processing addendum. We'll include our standard DPA and security addendum.

[33:40] Aisha: One last thing on separation: for multi-tenant hosted customers how do you guarantee no cross-tenant leakage, especially with shared model runtimes?
[33:53] Jonah: Isolation is both logical and process-based. We use per-tenant namespaces, request-level tagging, and strict memory/kvcache isolation plus fuzz testing during onboarding. For customers wanting guaranteed isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.

[36:10] Priya: Procurement will want a list of required contractual clauses — can you share standard SLR, SOC exhibits and insurance?
[36:22] Maya: Yes, we'll share insurance, standard clauses, and options for custom terms.

[40:00] Aisha: Great — recap of next steps?
[40:06] Maya: I'll send the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, DPA and security addendum, and a pricing sheet for pilot and dedicated options. Jonah will prepare an architecture doc showing hosted vs dedicated vs private, and we should schedule a SE-led deep dive for week of 9/21 to run benchmarks.
[40:25] Aisha: We'll also share our network diagram and compliance contact.

[41:00] Liam: One quick clarifying Q — for exported logs do you provide guaranteed ordering and sequence numbers for replay during audit?
[41:10] Jonah: Yes, logs include sequence IDs and checksums; export bundles are signed.

[43:45] Aisha: For the CMK integration, is there an extra cost for HSM-backed keys?
[43:51] Maya: There may be additional licensing or HSM costs depending on the deployment; we'll put options in the pricing sheet.

[45:20] Priya: On contract timing — if we go forward after pilot, what's typical lead time for Dedicated deployment?
[45:28] Maya: Typical lead time is 6-12 weeks depending on capacity and network setup; we'll provide a more exact timeline after scoping. Private on-prem can be longer due to procurement.

[48:00] Maya: Okay, thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with SOC links and initial pricing. Jonah will send the architecture doc mid next week. Anything else?
[48:12] Aisha: No, that's good. Appreciate it.
[48:18] Liam: Thanks all.
[48:20] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Call ended ~15:52 PDT
